title: Install two hook-in gondola brackets at a marked height and seat the steel shelf
instruction: Install both steel shelf brackets in the yellow-marked level-3 slots of the upright and seat the white shelf flat across them.
context: Stockers and order fillers (2.8M US workers) and general maintenance workers (1.5M) regularly reposition hook-in gondola shelf brackets to planogram heights: each bracket must be pitched nose-up so its lower tongue clears the bridge while its upper hook enters the slot, then swung flat before both hands seat the wide flanged shelf.
setup: Station table (top at z = 0.7475 m; x forward from the arm bases, y left). Fixed at the back is a dark powder-coated steel retail gondola upright, 340 mm wide and 232 mm tall on an 8 mm steel baseplate, with two vertical slotted standards centred at y = +0.120 m and y = -0.120 m whose 4.5 mm front webs lie at x = 0.410 m in front of 26 mm hollow channel cavities. Each standard has five rectangular slots, 11 mm wide and 19 mm tall on a 36 mm vertical pitch (sills at 44, 80, 116, 152 and 188 mm above the table), forming four bracket levels labelled 1 to 4; level 3 (upper sill at 152 mm, lower slot at 116 mm) is marked in yellow across both standards. Resting upright in fixed dark steel U-cradles at y = +0.245 m and y = -0.245 m (floor 42 mm up, rear shoulder at x = 0.365 m) are two loose galvanized stamped-steel gondola brackets (0.16 kg each, 5 mm blade, 188 mm overall length, 48 mm deep rear bearing heel, stepped 18 mm wide top support flange spanning 124 mm, blue vinyl-sleeved 28 x 12 x 25 mm front grip tab). Each bracket has a rear upper J-hook (10.5 mm neck with a 6.5 mm downward tooth behind the web) and a lower alignment tongue (6.5 mm long, 26.5 mm below the upper sill). Between the arms at (0.138, 0.000) m, resting flat 56 mm above the table on two fixed dark risers clear in front of the upright, is a loose white powder-coated steel shelf pan (0.42 kg, 320 mm wide by 146 mm deep, 4 mm deck, 7 mm downward captive front and rear lips leaving a 138 mm pocket, and 28 mm tall upright side fences 8 mm thick along both ends).
scoring: 0 if at any step a physical collider vertex of either bracket or the shelf makes contact (within 0.8 mm) with the station tabletop (z = 0.7475 m) or floor (z = -0.0125 m) with a pre-impact downward speed exceeding 0.50 m/s (an unsupported drop of more than ~1.3 cm); 0 unless every physical collider vertex of both brackets and the shelf moved under 1 mm (3D Euclidean distance) over the last 1.0 s (21 samples at 20 Hz). Temporary tilts, controlled near-misses above the surface, slow carries, or gentle placement on the table at 0.50 m/s or less do not penalize the trial. Otherwise, in the final state: 0.25 for each bracket seated in its column's level-3 slot and released (rear shoulder within 7 mm of x = 0.410 m, column y and the 152 mm level-3 sill, upper hook tooth behind the 4.5 mm web, lower tongue inside the 116 mm slot, orientation within 7 degrees of upright and square, and all fingertips at least 8 cm from every collider surface of the bracket), giving 0.50 when both brackets are seated at level 3. 1.0 if both brackets are seated at level 3, the white shelf rests directly across them (centre within 12 mm of x = 0.329 m, 15 mm of y = 0.000 m and 10 mm of 157 mm above the table, both bracket flanges captured inside the 138 mm lip pocket within 5 mm vertically of the deck underside, tilt 5 degrees or less, yaw within 6 degrees), and every fingertip is at least 8 cm from every collider surface of both brackets and the shelf.
reset_notes: Lift the white shelf off the brackets back onto its two front risers, tilt each steel bracket nose-up ~25 degrees to unhook it from level 3, and stand both brackets upright in their side cradles. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX simulation with primitive box colliders. The upright, cradles and shelf risers are fixed; both steel brackets and the flanged shelf are free rigid bodies with the masses in the setup. Slots, hooks and tongues are modelled to the sizes given in the setup. The 4 mm shelf deck is thicker than real sheet steel so its contacts stay stable. Sheet-metal flex is absent.
